finding: Web Audio rendering, output-route selection, device-change handling, and physical audibility are separate evidence layers and must remain separately inspectable even when combined into one deployment-bound packet.
design_implication: A packet may classify aligned evidence as supported, but browser render progression or route binding alone must never be promoted into proof that a person heard sound. Contradictions remain first-class outputs.

primary_sources.title: Web Audio API 1.1
primary_sources.status: W3C First Public Working Draft, 5 November 2024
primary_sources.relevance: Defines AudioContext state, routing, sink selection, and output timestamp concepts.

primary_sources.title: Audio Output Devices API
primary_sources.relevance: Defines output-device selection semantics and privacy-sensitive device exposure.

primary_sources.title: Audio Output Devices API Editor's Draft
primary_sources.relevance: Current algorithm and event surface for output-device selection and changes.

evidence_strength: implementation-ready deterministic prototype with seven passing boundary tests; browser and physical-device execution not performed
uncertainty: Browser support and behavior remain implementation-dependent, especially on mobile Safari.
A valid packet structure cannot establish physical audibility without a physical heard/not-heard observation.
The prototype validates normalized evidence objects; adapters must still map existing repository artifacts into this schema.
falsification_routes: Supply mismatched session, commit, or deployment identities and confirm fail-closed rejection.
Supply advancing render evidence with a not-heard physical outcome and confirm contradiction preservation.
Change the output device after non-default binding without confirmed rebinding and confirm contradiction preservation.
Run the adapter against a physical iPhone Safari session and compare packet classification with the retained raw observations.
